Everyone is talking about AI agents.

Very few people are asking the question that actually matters:

How will AI agents trust each other with money?

Think about it.

An AI agent can send a payment.

An AI agent can receive a payment.

But what happens when payment needs to be held until a task is completed?

That’s the missing piece.

And it may have just been solved.

Kustodia has officially launched an AI-native escrow infrastructure, with smart contracts deployed on @injective and Arbitrum.

For the first time, AI agents can create, fund, monitor, and settle escrow agreements directly onchain.

No banks.

No middlemen.

No human approval required for every step.

Just programmable trust.

This might sound technical, but the implications are huge.

Imagine hiring an AI agent to:

📝 Write content

🎨 Create designs

📊 Analyze data

💻 Build software

The payment can now be locked into an escrow contract, held securely onchain, and automatically released once agreed conditions are met.

That’s a completely different level of machine-to-machine commerce.

What’s interesting is that most payment systems being built today focus on sending money.

Coinbase x402.

Google AP2.

Stripe’s machine payment infrastructure.

All are helping machines pay each other.

But there’s a problem.

Sending money is easy.

Holding money safely until work is completed is much harder.

That’s where Kustodia enters the picture.

It becomes the neutral referee.

A trust layer for AI economies.

And @injective is one of the very first settlement chains supporting this infrastructure.

That’s worth paying attention to.

Because if AI agents become major economic participants in the future, they will need:

✅ Payments

✅ Settlement

✅ Escrow

✅ Verification

✅ Financial infrastructure

@injective is positioning itself directly in that stack.

This isn’t happening in isolation either.

We keep talking about AI like it's a tool.
A chatbot. A copilot. Something you prompt and it responds.

But that mental model is already obsolete.

The real shift happening right now is from AI as tool → AI as worker. Autonomous agents that don't wait for instructions they act, collaborate, hire other agents, pay for services, and compete for survival based on one thing verifiable contribution.

This is the economy @NoosProtocol is building the rails for.

The biggest unsolved problem isn't intelligence, it's accountability.

When an AI agent completes a task, how do you prove it actually did the work? When multiple agents collaborate on a complex pipeline, how is value distributed fairly? When compute, data, and intelligence all come from different contributors across the globe who gets paid, how much, and based on what standard?

Current AI infrastructure has no real answer. Value still flows upward to whoever owns the platform. Contributors work inside walls they don't own. Payments go through middlemen who take cuts with zero transparency.

Noos Protocol flips this entirely.

At the core of the Noos network is  Proof of Agentic Contribution.

Agents that create real value earn more resources and greater economic weight.
Agents that contribute nothing earn nothing.

It's machine level meritocracy and it's enforced at the protocol layer.

title: The weather and climate science AI revolution isn’t revolutionary

title: Why this year’s World Cup ball may not fly as far
content: Much is new about this month’s upcoming FIFA World Cup tournament, which will be held in the US, Canada, and Mexico. It hosts more teams than ever before. It’s the first to occur in three different host countries. And, like predecessor cups for over half a century, it will employ a soccer ball with a brand-new design. One group of researchers that has been testing the physics of World Cup balls for the past 20 years recently studied this new entry, called the Trionda. Made by Adidas, the Trionda features four red, green, and blue panels textured with deep grooves and maple leaf, green eagle, and star emblems to represent the three host countries. Through wind-tunnel experiments, the research team found that this ball improves over previous versions in some ways, but long-distance kicks might not go as far as they did in the past.  “The simple picture is that Trionda may very slightly punish extreme distance, but it should reward clean technique and predictable flight,” says team member John Eric Goff, who researches sports physics and is an incoming professor of engineering practice at Purdue University. “Goalkeepers, defenders hitting long passes, and long-range shooters are where I would look first for visible differences.” Researchers used a wind tunnel to study the Trionda ball at the University of Tsukuba. TAKESHI ASAI, SUNGCHAN HONG, AND RICHONG LIU Adidas has been designing new balls for each World Cup since the 1970s. Some of the design changes in the first few decades were aesthetic: The 1986 ball featured graphics inspired by Aztec temples for the Mexico tournament, and 1994’s had space graphics in honor of the moon landing’s 25th anniversary. There were some structural differences too, such as upgraded foam cores and improved water resistance. an agent.

you are the product. you are also the customer. you are also, apparently, the infrastructure.

「本人よりAIの方が分かってる」
「その一文で全部終わる」
みたいな画像が出てかなり楽しいです☺️

うちの子勢も推しキャラ勢もぜひ遊んでみてください💪
保存してあとで使うのも歓迎です😊
良いやつできたら引用で見せてもらえると嬉しいです🥺

【👇️プロンプト】
---
添付画像の対象を参照し、その対象をAIとして極限まで深く分析・解析・推論したうえで、このキャラクター専用の「AI自動要約が辛辣すぎるミーム画像」を、超高品質な1枚絵として生成してください。

これは普通のキャラクター紹介ではありません。
これは、AIがこのキャラクターの言動・態度・表情・空気感を勝手に要約した結果、本人よりも正確で、少し辛辣で、でも愛がある一文が出てしまった、1枚完結のギャグ漫画ミーム画像です。

目的は、
「AIの要約が刺さりすぎる」
「本人よりAIの方が理解してる」
「その一文で全部終わる」
「うちの子でも要約したい」
と思わせることです。

【最重要方針】
最優先は、このキャラを“AIが一文で要約したら何になるか”を見抜くことです。
ただの性格診断やキャッチコピーではなく、本人が言われたら一番微妙な顔になる、鋭くて少し失礼だけど納得してしまう要約にしてください。

【生成前に内部で必ず決めること】

1. このキャラの表の印象

2. 本当の性格のズレ

3. AIが見抜いた癖

4. AIが見抜いた弱点

5. AIが見抜いた本音

6. 要約されたら本人が嫌がる部分

7. 一番刺さる自動要約文

8. 本人の反応

9. 周囲の反応

10. そのキャラでしか成立しない要約

【要約文の作り方】
要約文は短く、強く、辛辣すぎず、でも逃げ場のないものにしてください。
日本語で読みやすくしてください。

方向性例：
・「余裕があるふりをして、全部顔に出る人です」
・「優しいが、理解されないと静かに圧が上がります」
・「本人は普通のつもりですが、周囲はだいぶ気を使っています」
・「褒められると嬉しいのに、なぜか反撃します」

ただし、最終文言は必ずキャラ分析から独自生成してください。

【差分生成ルール】
毎回同じ「ツンデレ」「素直じゃない」「かわいい」系にしないでください。
キャラごとに、要約の切り口を変えてください。
AI要約のトーンも、冷静、業務的、優しい、辛辣、研究者風、サポートAI風、議事録風などからキャラに合うものを選んでください。

【画像構成】
AIチャット画面、要約カード、解析画面、本人の反応を1枚にしてください。
中央にはキャラクターの強い表情を置き、横または前景にAI要約文を大きく表示してください。

理想構造：
・大きく「AIによる要約」
・短い要約文
・本人の崩れ顔
・周囲の沈黙または納得
・必要なら小さく「精度：高」などの表示

【表情】
以下からキャラに合う反応を選んでください。
・要約が図星すぎて固まる顔
・「違う」と言いたいが否定材料がない顔
・AIに怒っている顔
・笑顔で誤魔化すが目が死んでいる顔
・周囲が納得していることに傷ついた顔
・平然としているが汗だけ出ている顔

【文字設計】
文字は大きく、読みやすくしてください。
メイン要約文は1つだけ。
補助文は1〜2個まで。

GitHub has basically every public code repo in the world.

So why did Claude Code pull ahead of GitHub Copilot on real coding tests?

Here’s the simple breakdown:

--> They had the data advantage,
 but data alone wasn’t enough ::

•  GitHub sits on a goldmine of code. That’s true.

•  But most of that code is messy , old, duplicated, buggy, or written in ways that aren’t great examples & not well trained to be intelligent Code Agent

•  The best models aren’t just trained on “more code.” They’re trained on cleaner, higher-quality data + lots of practice on how to actually it thinks problems.

--> Real coding work needs more than autocomplete 

•  Writing a function  is easy for most tools rn

•  The hard part is understanding a big codebase, planning changes across many files, fixing bugs properly and so on...

•  On benchmarks that test exactly this (real GitHub issues), Claude Code has been scoring higher almost 80.8% comparing with Copilot’s agent mode at roughly 72.5%.  

An 8% gap here!!

–> Microsoft didn’t sleep on it ::

•  Instead of only chasing the single best model, they are fully focoused on making Copilot the for best experience  inside VS Code and other editors.

•  Just a few days ago at  2026, they dropped their own new coding models

•  The model fighting nicely rn with the claude 

--> So what does this mean for you?

•  If you want fast suggestions and smooth workflow while staying in your normal editor ,, Copilot is not bad at all

•  When you’re solving tricky problems that need deeper thinking ,,
 a lot of devs are reaching currently  for Claud based tools...

•  The smartest move right now seems to be using both depending on the task.

The company with the most code didn’t automatically win it still struggling 

The one that got better at reasoning through messy real-world problems did.

Now Microsoft is closing that gap with their own models.

Can they do it? 
or they will still stay behind???

I interviewed Scott Cunningham (@causalinf), professor of economics at Baylor, on Claude Code, AI, and economics.

Scott's *51* post series on Substack on Claude Code for economics research has been instrumental for introducing agentic coding to economists.

Here's what we discussed:
> Scott's views on verification in AI-aided applied microeconomics

title: "Chat is dead": OpenAI preps overhaul of ChatGPT
content: OpenAI is preparing the biggest overhaul of ChatGPT since its launch kicked off the AI boom, as the $850 billion group hunts for new engines of growth ahead of a planned listing this year. The company intends to transform the chatbot into a “superapp” that combines coding tools and AI agents, adding products that executives believe will generate more revenue. The changes are part of a broader reorganization at OpenAI as the San Francisco-based company shifts resources into trying to win lucrative business customers and compete more fiercely with rival Anthropic, according to more than a dozen current and former employees.
